nodes.name: A repository is not a product.
nodes.text: ## A repository is not a product.

nodes.name: Tools often treat a repository as the boundary of…
nodes.text: Tools often treat a repository as the boundary of everything: its own settings, its own docs, its own permissions. That works until a product grows a second repository. Then the brand guidelines exist twice, the naming rules drift apart, and an agent working in the iOS app never sees the decision made in the web app.

nodes.name: A startup’s product commonly spans a web app, a shared…
nodes.text: A startup’s product commonly spans a web app, a shared core, mobile apps and extensions. Those are different projects with different rules. They are also one product, with one name, one voice and many shared decisions.

nodes.name: NullDull uses a small hierarchy. The **workspace** is the…
nodes.text: NullDull uses a small hierarchy. The **workspace** is the organization: its members, teams and organization-wide resources. A **project** is a component or workstream—web, core, iOS, Android, extensions—with its own files and configuration. Projects sit directly under the workspace by default.

nodes.name: **Products** are an optional middle level for agencies and…
nodes.text: **Products** are an optional middle level for agencies and companies with several products. They are off for new workspaces; owners and admins can turn them on under Workspace settings → General. A product groups related projects and holds the resources they share, such as product-wide guidance, logos or a publishing surface.

nodes.name: Each resource has one owning location. Workspace-wide…
nodes.text: Each resource has one owning location. Workspace-wide rules live at the workspace root. Product-wide decisions live at the product. Project instructions live with the project. A project task can draw on all of them without anything being copied.

nodes.name: Root and project instruction files stay distinct. A…
nodes.text: Root and project instruction files stay distinct. A project’s `AGENTS.md` supplements the shared one; local sync never overwrites one with the other. And access follows the same structure: assignments at a workspace, product or project provide defaults for the files inside, the nearest location wins, and an explicit file-level rule overrides them all.

nodes.name: A checkout on your machine is not a project’s identity.…
nodes.text: A checkout on your machine is not a project’s identity. Folder names change, people clone into different paths, and a repository can be moved. NullDull treats local directories as mappings to a project rather than as the project itself, so renaming a checkout does not create a new project.

nodes.name: The CLI follows the same idea. Each workspace keeps its…
nodes.text: The CLI follows the same idea. Each workspace keeps its own login, and login binds the directory it runs in to the approved workspace; subdirectories inherit the nearest binding. Two projects that use different workspaces stay signed in at the same time. Folders in Memory can carry a preferred repository and path, so files land in the same place for everyone.

nodes.name: When you choose a location in the app, Memory, Grid and…
nodes.text: When you choose a location in the app, Memory, Grid and Locale all follow it. Switching from a project’s Memory files to its Grid pages keeps you in the same place. If an app can’t show that location—because it isn’t set up there, or you don’t have access—it falls back to the nearest location it can show, without changing your selection.

nodes.name: The point is not the hierarchy for its own sake. It is…
nodes.text: The point is not the hierarchy for its own sake. It is that a team describes its product once, in the shape it actually has, and every person and agent finds the same context from wherever they start.
